subject: [PATCH v5 02/12] mm/page_alloc: keep the pagesets of an empty zone

reviews.author: Zi Yan
reviews.summary:
Gave Reviewed-by

Reviewer Zi Yan suggested that the patch should include an explanation for why zone->per_cpu_pageset can only be NULL at boot time, and requested initialization of this variable.
reviews.raw_body:
it might be better to explain zone->per_cpu_pageset can only be NULL at
boot time and it needs an initialization.

2026-11-01.patch_summary: This patch prevents the pagesets of an empty zone from being freed prematurely, which can cause corruption when a new owner takes over the per-cpu memory. Instead, it keeps the existing pagesets and allows setup_zone_pageset() to reuse them. This fix addresses a problem introduced by a previous commit that freed the pagesets when a zone became empty.

reviews.author: Vlastimil (SUSE)
reviews.summary: Reviewer Vlastimil suggested simplifying the check in setup_zone_pageset() by removing the explicit comparison to &boot_pageset, as it is unnecessary and would simply set the same values already present.

reviews.author: Zi Yan
reviews.summary: Reviewer Zi Yan noted that the patch causes zone_pcp_init() to become a no-op for free_area_init_core_hotplug(), and questioned whether zone_init_internals() is still needed for hotplug, suggesting this issue belongs to a later cleanup.
reviews.raw_body:
Right. And zone_pcp_init(), called by zone_init_internals(), becomes a nop for
free_area_init_core_hotplug(). Then I wonder if zone_init_internals() is
needed for hotplug, but that belongs to a later cleanup.


-- 
Best Regards,
Yan, Zi
